sc: OFC crossing centiles, tense fontanelle, wide sutures, sunset eyes → Hydrocephalus: ultrasound, VP shunt
Child with a VP shunt: vomiting, headache, drowsy → Shunt blockage
Lumbosacral sac with cord, flaccid legs, patulous anus → Myelomeningocele
f: Obstructive (aqueduct stenosis, tumour, Chiari) · communicating (after TB or bacterial meningitis, haemorrhage)
Big head crossing centiles · bulging fontanelle · wide sutures · sunset eyes · older: headache, vomiting, papilloedema
Cranial ultrasound (open fontanelle) · CT/MRI · toxoplasma, CMV if congenital
VP shunt · endoscopic third ventriculostomy · shunt problems: blockage, infection (first 6 months)
Occulta (hair tuft) · meningocele (CSF only) · myelomeningocele (cord: paralysis, bladder, bowel, hydrocephalus 80–90%) · close in 48–72 h
Folic acid 0.4 mg/day before conception · 5 mg if previous NTD or on valproate
trap: Big head with normal ventricles and a big-headed parent = familial macrocephaly · hydrocephalus + chorioretinitis + calcification = toxoplasmosis · raised maternal AFP → scan for NTD
